microwave_time.user_tendencies: IF eating alone in quiet personal setting AND neutral affective state THEN 2 min BECAUSE moderate warmth is comfortable. IF food is fruit or cold dessert THEN no microwave BECAUSE intended serving temperature is cold. IF user is fatigued or in a hurry THEN 1 min BECAUSE reduced wait time outweighs minor temperature preference. IF user is relaxed with ample time AND eating warm foods THEN 3 min BECAUSE extended warmth enhances comfort and palatability when time is not a constraint.

robot_speed.user_tendencies: IF eating alone in quiet personal setting AND neutral affective state THEN medium BECAUSE balanced between comfort and efficiency. IF user is in a hurry THEN fast BECAUSE reduces meal duration. IF user is fatigued AND (eating alone OR affective state is relaxed) THEN slow BECAUSE reduced cognitive load from slower movements aids comfort when energy is limited. IF eating in social setting AND user is fatigued THEN fast BECAUSE effort minimization (less attentional demand) takes priority over social comfort in this tie-break context. IF user is energetic THEN fast BECAUSE user is less sensitive to movement speed when energized.

skewering_axis.user_tendencies: IF eating alone in quiet personal setting AND neutral affective state THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE improves bite acquisition success. IF user has wide mouth opening capability (as described) AND food is firm or difficult to skewer THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE wide mouth opening accommodates larger bites. IF food is soft or delicate (e.g., fruit, dessert) AND user prefers controlled bites THEN parallel to major axis BECAUSE produces narrower bites even though user has good mouth opening. IF eating in social setting AND user is fatigued THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE minimizing retry attempts takes priority over bite size preference in fatigue contexts.

IF user is fatigued THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE eliminates need for forward lean coordination which would be effortful given severe upper-limb paralysis and trunk control limitations. User's physical profile (lack of trunk control) makes inside-mouth transfer the only viable mode across all contexts.

bite_dipping_preference.user_tendencies: IF eating alone in quiet personal setting AND neutral affective state AND food has sauce THEN more BECAUSE user can enjoy enhanced flavor without social messiness concerns. IF eating in social setting AND food has sauce AND user is not fatigued THEN less BECAUSE reduces messiness and dripping that might be socially awkward in front of others. IF user is fatigued (regardless of social context) AND food has sauce THEN more BECAUSE flavor enhancement may aid palatability when energy is low; user less concerned with messiness when fatigued. IF food is fruit or cold dessert without sauces THEN do not dip BECAUSE no dippable items available. IF user is in a hurry AND food has sauce THEN less BECAUSE reduces risk of dripping delays and cleanup. IF user is relaxed with ample time AND eating alone AND food has sauce THEN more BECAUSE user can fully enjoy sauce without time pressure.

bite_ordering.default: Alternate between protein and vegetables, dipping protein items in sauce and vegetables without dipping.
bite_ordering.user_tendencies: IF eating alone in quiet personal setting AND neutral affective state THEN predict ordering based on user's stated preferences if known; otherwise no particular order. IF eating in social setting AND user is not fatigued THEN order items to minimize messiness (less-saucy items before sauce-dipped items to reduce visual dripping in front of others). IF user is fatigued THEN order easiest-to-consume items first to reduce effort while energy is depleting; save firmer or more effortful items for later if acceptable. IF food includes soft items (fruit, dessert) and firm items (meat, vegetables) AND user is fatigued THEN present soft items first because they require less mastication effort when user is fatigued. IF user is in a hurry THEN order items by acquisition difficulty (easiest-to-pick items first) to maximize meal speed and reduce retry risk. IF food has multiple sauces AND user prefers specific pairings (e.g., chicken with sauce A, vegetables with sauce B) THEN maintain pairings as specified; otherwise pair saucy items at end to contain mess.

IF user is in a hurry THEN 15 sec BECAUSE shorter timeout reduces meal duration. IF eating in social setting AND user is not fatigued THEN 60 sec BECAUSE longer timeout provides ample time for explicit confirmation or intervention without rushing in social context where social partner may be conversing. IF user is fatigued (regardless of social context) THEN 30 sec BECAUSE shorter timeout reduces fatigue-related attentional demands; 15 sec may be too aggressive if user needs momentary recovery pause. IF user is relaxed with ample time THEN 60 sec BECAUSE extended timeout accommodates unhurried decision-making and reduces cognitive pressure. IF user is watching television or distracted by other activity THEN 60 sec BECAUSE longer timeout compensates for divided attention and competing cognitive demands.
